v.q: How can the Redux state be changed?
o: By editing the reducer at runtime
v.w: The store is read-only. Every change is an action that a reducer handles.

v.q: What does a Redux action describe?
v.w: By convention it is { type, payload }, named like cart/itemAdded.

v.q: Why must a reducer not mutate state?
v.w: A mutated object keeps the same reference, so selectors and React see no change.

v.q: Which is allowed in a reducer?
v.w: A reducer is a pure function with no side effects.

v.q: What does Immer let you do inside createSlice?
o: Write code that looks like mutation
v.w: It records changes on a draft and produces a new immutable state.
Action types follow the slice name, such as accounts/accountFrozen.
The slice handles them in extraReducers to set loading, data and error.

v.q: Where should a network call be made in Redux?
o: In a thunk or RTK Query
v.w: Reducers must stay pure, so effects live outside them.

v.q: Why does a selector using state.items.filter(...) re-render on every dispatch?
o: It returns a new array each time
v.w: useSelector compares by reference, and a new array never equals the old one.
It recomputes only when its input selectors return different values.

v.q: What does normalised state look like?
o: Entities by id plus a list of ids
v.w: createEntityAdapter generates this shape and its selectors.

v.q: What is a benefit of normalising?
v.w: Updating by id is O(1) and the data cannot drift between copies.

v.q: How is the RTK Query cache keyed?
v.w: Components asking for the same key share one request and one entry.

v.q: What makes a list refetch after a mutation?
v.w: providesTags and invalidatesTags connect queries and mutations.

v.q: Where should server data (lists, details) usually live?
v.w: Keep only real client state in Redux.

v.q: Which state is a poor fit for Redux?
o: Text typed into a form field
A cart used on many pages
v.w: Form input is local and short-lived. Keep it in the component or a form library.
